sources.entry: Xit - Xit is a graphical tool for working with git repositories.

summary.one_liner: Xit is a visual Git client for macOS-style repository browsing, built as a rewrite of GitX and currently in beta.
summary.what_it_does: Xit is a graphical tool for viewing and managing git repositories. Its sidebar lists branches, remotes, tags, submodules, and stashes. The history list shows a graph of commits and branches, can be searched by author, message content, or hash, and lets you move back and forward through previously selected commits. File lists show changed files or a full outline hierarchy at any commit. Files can be previewed as diffs, blame, plain text, or QuickLook previews, and the blame view color-codes lines changed at the same time and links to their source commits. The stated goals emphasize handling large repositories with many commits and files.
use_cases: view git history as a commit graph
browse branches, tags, and stashes in a sidebar
search commits by author or message
see blame annotations for a file
preview file diffs at a past commit
manage a large git repository visually
how_to_run: See CONTRIBUTING.md in the repository for build and contribution instructions
stack: Swift (implied by macOS-app listing; not named in README)
notable: Rewrite of the GitX client with a focus on a cleaner, unit-tested codebase
Blame view color-codes lines changed together and links back to their commits
Commit history graph with search by author, message, or hash
Previews include diffs, blame, plain text, and QuickLook
caveats: Currently in beta; most basic features are in place but the 1.0 milestone is not yet reached
Online service integration such as GitHub is planned but not yet available
Interactive rebase and more robust push/pull and merge conflict handling are roadmap items, not current features
